subject: english-language
title: Headlines and Hooks
welcome_lead: Newspapers and websites fight for your click.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on headlines, captions and media hooks.
final_note: You can now analyse a headline for technique and intent.

walkthroughs.body_html: Headlines often use puns or alliteration: 'Crumbs! Local Baker Crowned'. Short, punchy, memorable.
Clickbait overstates or hides the point ('You'll never believe what happened!'). Effective but trust-corroding.
Captions sit under images; pull quotes blow up a striking line to draw the eye into the article.

What is the IPA in linguistics?
options: The IPA is just another alphabet like the Roman or Greek alphabet.
Overextension is when children speak too loudly.
The International Phonetic Alphabet — a standardised set of symbols where each symbol represents one distinct sound. Used to transcribe pronunciation precisely across all languages.
The IPA stands for International Phonetic Acronym.

mcqs.q: What is an adjacency pair in conversation analysis?
options: Overextension is when children speak too loudly.
Adjacency pairs are two people who sit next to each other while talking.
A two-part sequence where the first part conditions the second — question/answer, greeting/greeting, request/acceptance-or-refusal. The second part is 'conditionally relevant' on the first.
Adjacency pairs are pairs of synonyms in vocabulary lists.

mcqs.q: What is overextension in child language?
options: The IPA stands for International Phonetic Acronym.
When a child applies a word more broadly than adults do — e.g. calling all four-legged animals 'dog' before learning distinct categories.
Overextension is when children speak too loudly.
Overextension is when children use very long words they don't understand.
